Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the initial packet on the identity questionnaire. A couple of follow-ups from our security and identity owners before we proceed to procurement:

- How does delegated admin work for cross-tenant support teams; specifically, can we limit admin sessions to IP ranges and require MFA for elevated operations?

We appreciate quick answers; procurement is asking for 72-hour turnaround.

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: clarifications on SSO / SCIM / admin controls

Samir —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect 1.0, including custom attribute mappings (we commonly map eduPerson*). SCIM v2 is supported with delta events and granular filtering; we also support bulk provisioning via SCIM bulk where customers need it. Delegated admin supports role-based RBAC with session policies (IP allowlists, session MFA enforcement) and audit trails exportable to CSV/JSON.

I attached a short package: bluepeak_sso_matrix_v1.xlsx (protocols + attribute examples), scim_delta_examples.yml (sample payloads and webhook sequence), rbac_role_map.csv (example role hierarchy), and evidence_screenshots.zip (console flows and audit export).

Below are the concrete answers to each item you called out:

1) SSO protocols and attributes:
- SAML 2.0: SP-initiated and IdP-initiated. Support for NameID formats, custom SAML assertions, and SHA-256 signing. We accept arbitrary attribute maps and can preserve eduPersonPrincipalName and eduPersonAffiliation.
- OIDC: full claims mapping, including support for requested scopes, custom claim transformation, and dynamic client registration for internal partners.
- Attribute mapping example (from our mapping sheet):
    - eduPersonPrincipalName -> user.username
    - mail -> user.email
    - eduPersonAffiliation -> user.attributes.affiliations (list)

2) SCIM provisioning:
- SCIM v2 endpoint supporting incremental (delta) syncs via change tokens and polling, plus optional events webhooks for near-real-time provisioning.
- Filtering: RFC 7644-style filters supported (e.g., filter=groups eq "shipped-team"), and we support paging and server-side filtering to avoid full-scan syncs.
- Large tenant considerations: our connector supports resume tokens and checkpointed delta ranges; customers with >100k users typically run a one-time bulk import then switch to delta syncs.

3) RBAC and delegated admin:
- Role model: hierarchical roles + resource-scoped permissions; roles can be applied at org, tenant, or dataset scope.
- Delegated admin: create admin groups with scoped privileges; elevation can be configured to require step-up MFA and IP restrictions.
- Session controls: session MFA required for role elevation; admin session TTL is configurable (default 1 hour).

4) Audit, logs, and evidence:
- Audit logs capture actor, action, target, timestamp, and session metadata (IP, user-agent). Retention: 13 months by default; longer retention via add-on.
- Exports: ad-hoc CSV/JSON export and streaming to customer SIEM (Syslog/HTTPS) or cloud storage (S3).

5) Key management and isolation:
- Customer-managed keys supported via AWS KMS & Azure Key Vault for encryption of stored secrets. HSM-backed support for Private deployments.

If you want, we can schedule a short technical call where Kim Park (product security) and Ben Carter (identity integrations) walk through the console and the SCIM delta example.

Next steps: confirm whether you want a live demo or a recorded walkthrough; we can also provide an ephemeral test tenant for your engineering team.

Thanks,

Lina / Samir —

Attached is a redacted audit_export_mar2028.csv (included inside evidence_screenshots.zip) showing typical audit columns: timestamp, actor_id, actor_email (redacted), action, target_type, target_id, ip_address (redacted), session_id. We removed PII and anonymized identifiers.

On nested groups: our SCIM connector supports group objects with members that are other groups (Group-membership with "members" referencing group IDs). For most AD/Okta customers we recommend using group expansion during provisioning (i.e., resolve nested groups on the IdP side and push a flattened membership to Redwood) to simplify permissions evaluation at runtime. That said, Redwood's role sync supports both flattened membership imports and nested group references — our role-evaluation engine will traverse up to 3 levels of nesting by default and can be configured for deeper traversals in Dedicated or Private deployments.

Quick configuration notes we included in scim_delta_examples.yml:
- changeType: "update" (user with added group)
- group object example: { "displayName": "engineering:platform", "members": [ { "value": "grp-001" }, { "value": "grp-002" } ] }
- recommended pattern: flatten on IdP for high-volume tenants; enable server-side expansion when you rely on nested-groups semantics.

We can provide a 30-minute walkthrough and provision a timeboxed test tenant with sample data and a SCIM webhook sink so your team can validate delta semantics and nested-group behavior.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Identity Integrations
Redwood Inference
